finding.claim: Webhook callback URL supplied by a client at POST /subscribe is stored with no validation. The server later POSTs the payload to it every minute, so an attacker can make the server send requests to internal hosts, loopback, or cloud metadata endpoints. The scheme and host are unrestricted, and DNS rebinding is not mitigated. The response is discarded, so this is blind SSRF with an attacker-influenced POST body.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL from the request body
URL is stored unvalidated in the static subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates over every stored callback URL on the per-minute job
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no scheme, host, or IP checks
client.send issues the POST to the attacker-chosen destination

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, resolved-IP check for private, loopback, or link-local ranges, or DNS pinning exists anywhere on the path. Nothing in this file authenticates the caller of subscribe. HttpClient.newHttpClient() follows no redirects by default, which is not a mitigation here. The response body is read but not returned, so the SSRF is blind. The payload is server-defined, but the attacker controls the destination host, port, and path. A request such as http://169.254.169.254/... is reachable, though a POST to IMDS has limited use (IMDSv2 token PUT is not possible). Internal POST-accepting services remain exposed.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 builds the URI from it and sends the POST, with no scheme, host or IP check. The only regex guard (line 30) protects thumb(), not this path. The repo has no routing or auth code, so I could not confirm how /subscribe is exposed, but nothing restricts the caller.
